name: Chisholm v. Georgia
description: Held that states could be sued in federal court by citizens of other states, leading to the 11th Amendment.

name: Calder v. Bull
description: Defined the Ex Post Facto Clause as applying only to criminal laws and not to civil matters.

name: Marbury v. Madison
description: Established the principle of judicial review, granting the Supreme Court power to declare laws unconstitutional.

name: Martin v. Hunter's Lessee
description: Affirmed the Supreme Court's authority to review state court decisions involving federal law.

name: McCulloch v. Maryland
description: Interpreted the Necessary and Proper Clause broadly and affirmed federal supremacy over state taxation.

name: Corfield v. Coryell
description: Early circuit court case defining 'privileges and immunities' to include the right to travel and acquire property.

name: Gibbons v. Ogden
description: Defined federal commerce power broadly to include navigation, asserting it as superior to state regulations.

name: Barron v. City of Baltimore
description: Held that the Bill of Rights originally applied only to the federal government and not to the states.

name: Prigg v. Pennsylvania
description: Held that federal law regarding the return of enslaved people superseded state personal liberty laws.

name: Luther v. Borden
description: Established the political question doctrine regarding the enforcement of the Republican Form of Government Clause.

name: Dred Scott v. Sandford
description: Ruled that Black people were not citizens and that Congress could not prohibit slavery in federal territories.

name: Prize Cases
description: Affirmed the President’s power to take military action during an insurrection without a formal declaration of war.

name: Ex Parte Milligan
description: Ruled that citizens cannot be tried by military tribunals when civilian courts are still functioning.

name: Mississippi v. Johnson
description: Held that the President could not be restrained by an injunction from carrying out his executive duties.

name: Hepburn v. Griswold
description: One of the Paper Money Cases that initially ruled the Legal Tender Act unconstitutional as applied to prior debts.

name: Knox v. Lee
description: Reversed Hepburn v. Griswold, ruling that the Legal Tender Act was a valid exercise of federal power.

name: Slaughterhouse Cases
description: Narrowly interpreted the 14th Amendment’s Privileges or Immunities Clause, limiting its impact on state regulations.

name: Bradwell v. Illinois
description: Upheld a state's refusal to license a woman to practice law, reflecting a restrictive view of the 14th Amendment.

name: United States v. Cruikshank
description: Held that the 14th Amendment protects only against state action, not private acts of violence or conspiracy.

name: Reynolds v. United States
description: Established that while religious belief is protected, religious conduct that violates neutral laws is not.

name: Strauder v. West Virginia
description: Struck down a law excluding Black citizens from juries as a violation of the Equal Protection Clause.

name: Civil Rights Cases
description: Held that Congress lacks the power to prohibit private racial discrimination under the 14th Amendment.

name: Elk v. Wilkins
description: Held that Native Americans born on reservations were not citizens under the 14th Amendment.

name: Yick Wo v. Hopkins
description: Held that a facially neutral law administered in a discriminatory manner violates the Equal Protection Clause.

name: Hans v. Louisiana
description: Extended state sovereign immunity to prevent a state from being sued in federal court by its own citizens.

name: In re Neagle
description: Affirmed the President's power to protect federal judges without an express statutory mandate.

name: United States v. E.C. Knight Co.
description: The Sugar Trust Case that limited commerce power by distinguishing manufacturing from interstate commerce.

name: Plessy v. Ferguson
description: Established the separate but equal doctrine, constitutionally upholding state-mandated racial segregation.

name: Chicago, Burlington & Quincy Railroad Co. v. Chicago
description: The first case to incorporate a protection from the Bill of Rights (Just Compensation) against the states.

name: Champion v. Ames
description: Held that the power to regulate commerce includes the ability to prohibit the transport of items across state lines.

name: Lochner v. New York
description: Struck down a limit on bakers' working hours as a violation of the freedom of contract.

name: Jacobson v. Massachusetts
description: Upheld the state’s power to enforce compulsory vaccination laws for the protection of public health.

name: Muller v. Oregon
description: Upheld a law limiting work hours for women, distinguishing it from Lochner based on perceived physical differences.

name: Hipolite Egg Co. v. United States
description: Upheld the Pure Food and Drug Act, allowing federal seizure of adulterated goods transported in interstate commerce.

name: Shreveport Rate Cases
description: Allowed federal regulation of intrastate rail rates that had a substantial effect on interstate commerce.

name: Selective Draft Law Cases
description: Upheld the military draft, ruling it did not violate the 13th Amendment or religious freedom.

name: Hammer v. Dagenhart
description: Struck down federal child labor laws as an unconstitutional intrusion into local state matters.

name: Schenck v. United States
description: Established the clear and present danger test for evaluating government restrictions on speech.

name: Adkins v. Children's Hospital
description: Struck down minimum wage laws for women as a violation of the freedom of contract.

name: Meyer v. Nebraska
description: Recognized the right of parents to direct the education of their children as a fundamental liberty.

name: Pierce v. Society of Sisters
description: Affirmed the right of parents to choose private or parochial schools for their children over public ones.

name: Buck v. Bell
description: Upheld state eugenics laws allowing forced sterilization of those deemed socially inadequate.

name: Gong Lum v. Rice
description: Upheld the racial segregation of a Chinese-American student in Mississippi under the separate but equal doctrine.

name: Wong Kim Ark
description: Established birthright citizenship under the 14th Amendment for children born in the U.S. to non-citizens.

name: Nebbia v. New York
description: Held that states can regulate prices for the public welfare, signaling a retreat from the Lochner era.

name: Schechter Poultry Corp. v. United States
description: Struck down New Deal codes as unconstitutional delegations of legislative authority to the executive branch.

name: Humphrey's Executor v. United States
description: Limited the President's power to remove heads of independent regulatory agencies at will.

name: United States v. Butler
description: Held that the federal government could not use the taxing and spending power to regulate local agricultural production.

name: West Coast Hotel v. Parrish
description: Upheld minimum wage laws, effectively ending the freedom of contract doctrine from the Lochner era.

name: NLRB v. Jones & Laughlin Steel Corp.
description: Expanded the Commerce Clause to allow federal regulation of local activities that substantially affect commerce.

name: United States v. Carolene Products
description: Established the rational basis test while hinting at higher scrutiny for protected groups in Footnote Four.

name: United States v. Darby
description: Overruled Hammer v. Dagenhart, confirming federal power to regulate labor conditions affecting interstate competition.

name: Wickard v. Filburn
description: Held that commerce power reaches purely local production if the aggregate effect impacts the national market.

name: Hirabayashi v. United States
description: Upheld a wartime curfew for Japanese Americans, citing military necessity.

name: Korematsu v. United States
description: Upheld Japanese American internment during wartime but established strict scrutiny for racial classifications.

name: Ex Parte Endo
description: Ruled that the government could not continue to detain a citizen whose loyalty had been established.

name: Ex Parte Quirin
description: Held that military tribunals could be used to try unlawful combatants who breached the laws of war.

name: United States v. South-Eastern Underwriters Ass'n
description: Held that the insurance industry is subject to the federal commerce power.

name: United Public Workers v. Mitchell
description: Upheld restrictions on the political activities of federal executive branch employees.

name: Shelley v. Kraemer
description: Held that judicial enforcement of private racially restrictive covenants is unconstitutional state action.

name: Railway Express Agency v. New York
description: Upheld a law regulating truck advertising as a valid exercise of police power under rational basis review.

name: Youngstown Sheet & Tube Co. v. Sawyer
description: Established the framework for evaluating executive power, ruling the President cannot seize private property without authority.

name: Brown v. Board of Education
description: Declared that racial segregation in public schools is unconstitutional, overruling separate but equal.

name: Bolling v. Sharpe
description: Held that the 5th Amendment's Due Process Clause requires racial equality in D.C. schools.

name: Lee Optical v. Williamson
description: Applied highly deferential rational basis review to a state economic regulation favoring opticians.

name: Sweezy v. New Hampshire
description: Reversed a contempt conviction for a professor, establishing core constitutional protections for academic freedom.

name: Cooper v. Aaron
description: Asserted that Supreme Court decisions are the supreme law of the land and bind all state officials.

name: Baker v. Carr
description: Ruled that challenges to legislative apportionment are justiciable and not excluded as political questions.

name: Sherbert v. Verner
description: Established that the state must have a compelling interest to deny benefits based on religious practices.

name: Heart of Atlanta Motel v. United States
description: Upheld the Civil Rights Act's ban on discrimination in public accommodations via the Commerce Clause.

name: Katzenbach v. McClung
description: Confirmed that federal civil rights laws apply to local businesses that purchase supplies through interstate commerce.

name: Griswold v. Connecticut
description: Found a constitutional right to privacy that protects the use of contraceptives by married couples.

name: United States v. Brown
description: Struck down a law prohibiting members of the Communist Party from serving as labor union officers as a bill of attainder.

name: Katzenbach v. Morgan
description: Upheld federal power to protect voting rights regardless of state literacy requirements under the 14th Amendment.

name: South Carolina v. Katzenbach
description: Upheld the Voting Rights Act of 1965 as a valid exercise of Congress's power to enforce the 15th Amendment.

name: Loving v. Virginia
description: Struck down laws prohibiting interracial marriage as a violation of equal protection and fundamental rights.

name: Keyishian v. Board of Regents
description: Struck down teacher loyalty oaths and recognized academic freedom as a core constitutional protection.

name: Lemon v. Kurtzman
description: Established the Lemon test for determining whether government action violates the Establishment Clause.

name: Roe v. Wade
description: Recognized a constitutional right to abortion based on a right to privacy derived from the 14th Amendment.

name: United States v. Nixon
description: Ruled that executive privilege is not absolute and cannot be used to withhold evidence from a criminal trial.

name: Milliken v. Bradley
description: Restricted court-ordered desegregation to within individual districts unless inter-district intent was shown.

name: Buckley v. Valeo
description: Upheld limits on political contributions but struck down limits on campaign expenditures as free speech violations.

name: Fitzpatrick v. Bitzer
description: Held that Congress can abrogate state sovereign immunity under its 14th Amendment enforcement powers.

name: Craig v. Boren
description: Established intermediate scrutiny as the standard of review for gender-based classifications.

name: Washington v. Davis
description: Held that proof of discriminatory intent is required to establish a violation of the Equal Protection Clause.

name: Mathews v. Eldridge
description: Established a balancing test to determine the procedural due process required before government action.

name: Hunt v. Washington State Apple Advertising Commission
description: Struck down a state law that discriminated against out-of-state producers under the Dormant Commerce Clause.

name: Regents of the Univ. of Cal. v. Bakke
description: Upheld the use of race as an admission factor while prohibiting fixed racial quotas.

name: Hicklin v. Orbeck
description: Struck down an Alaska Hire law as a violation of the Privileges and Immunities Clause of Article IV.

name: Hodel v. Virginia Surface Mining
description: Upheld federal surface mining regulations as a valid exercise of the commerce power.

name: Dames & Moore v. Regan
description: Upheld presidential orders suspending claims against Iran during a crisis, citing congressional acquiescence.

name: City of Los Angeles v. Lyons
description: Held that a plaintiff lacked standing to seek an injunction against police chokeholds without proof of future injury.

name: INS v. Chadha
description: Struck down the legislative veto as a violation of the requirements for bicameralism and presentment.

name: Allen v. Wright
description: Held that parents lacked standing to challenge IRS tax exemptions for discriminatory private schools.

name: Garcia v. San Antonio MTA
description: Held that federalism limits on commerce power are primarily maintained through the political process.

name: Maine v. Taylor
description: Upheld a state ban on imported baitfish under the Dormant Commerce Clause for environmental protection.

name: Morrison v. Olson
description: Upheld the Independent Counsel Act, ruling that it did not unconstitutionally interfere with executive power.

name: Texas v. Johnson
description: Ruled that flag burning is protected symbolic speech under the First Amendment.

name: Lujan v. Defenders of Wildlife
description: Articulated the modern standing test requiring injury-in-fact, causation, and redressability.

name: Planned Parenthood v. Casey
description: Affirmed the core right to abortion while replacing the trimester framework with the undue burden test.

name: New York v. United States
description: Held that the federal government cannot commandeer state legislatures by forcing them to enact specific laws.

name: Church of Lukumi Babalu Aye v. Hialeah
description: Struck down local ordinances that targeted the specific religious practice of animal sacrifice.

name: Wisconsin v. Mitchell
description: Upheld a penalty-enhancement statute for bias-motivated crimes against a First Amendment challenge.

name: United States v. Lopez
description: Struck down a federal law banning guns in schools for exceeding Congress's power under the Commerce Clause.

name: BMW v. Gore
description: Held that grossly excessive punitive damage awards violate the Due Process Clause.

name: Romer v. Evans
description: Struck down a state amendment targeting LGBTQ+ individuals for exclusion from anti-discrimination laws.

name: United States v. Virginia
description: Ruled that the male-only admissions policy of a state military college violated the Equal Protection Clause.

name: City of Boerne v. Flores
description: Held that Congress's 14th Amendment enforcement power is limited to congruence and proportionality.

name: Printz v. United States
description: Held that the federal government cannot commandeer state executive officials to implement federal laws.

name: Clinton v. City of New York
description: Struck down the Line Item Veto Act as a violation of the Presentment Clause.

name: Saenz v. Roe
description: Struck down state laws limiting welfare benefits for new residents as a violation of the right to travel.

name: Troxel v. Granville
description: Struck down a grandparent visitation statute that interfered with the fundamental rights of parents.

name: United States v. Morrison
description: Ruled that the Commerce Clause does not permit Congress to regulate non-economic violent crime.

name: Board of Trustees of the Univ. of Alabama v. Garrett
description: Held that the 11th Amendment prevents private individuals from suing states for money damages under the ADA.

name: Lawrence v. Texas
description: Ruled that the government cannot criminalize private, consensual sexual conduct between adults.

name: Nevada Dept. of Human Resources v. Hibbs
description: Upheld federal leave laws against state sovereign immunity as a remedy for gender discrimination.

name: Stogner v. California
description: Ruled that retroactively extending a statute of limitations to revive expired claims violates the Ex Post Facto Clause.

name: Tennessee v. Lane
description: Upheld the ADA's requirement for courthouse accessibility as a valid exercise of Section 5 power.

name: Gonzales v. Raich
description: Held that the Commerce Clause allows Congress to prohibit local cultivation and use of marijuana.

name: Hamdi v. Rumsfeld
description: Held that a U.S. citizen detained as an enemy combatant has a right to challenge his detention before a neutral decision-maker.

name: Rasul v. Bush
description: Ruled that federal courts have jurisdiction to hear habeas corpus petitions from foreign nationals at Guantanamo Bay.

name: Garcetti v. Ceballos
description: Held that public employees do not have First Amendment protection for speech made pursuant to official duties.

name: Massachusetts v. EPA
description: Recognized state standing to challenge federal inaction on climate change due to special solicitude.

name: District of Columbia v. Heller
description: Recognized an individual's right to keep and bear arms for self-defense within the home.

name: Boumediene v. Bush
description: Held that foreign nationals at Guantanamo Bay have a constitutional right to petition for habeas corpus.

name: McDonald v. City of Chicago
description: Incorporated the individual right to bear arms against state and local governments.

name: NFIB v. Sebelius
description: Upheld the ACA's individual mandate under the taxing power while limiting commerce power.

name: Shelby County v. Holder
description: Struck down the Voting Rights Act's coverage formula as an unconstitutional burden on state sovereignty.

name: Clapper v. Amnesty International USA
description: Held that plaintiffs lacked standing to challenge surveillance because their injury was speculative.

name: Obergefell v. Hodges
description: Ruled that the 14th Amendment requires all states to license and recognize same-sex marriages.

name: Zivotofsky v. Kerry
description: Held that the President has the exclusive authority to recognize foreign sovereigns and territories.

name: Gundy v. United States
description: Upheld a broad delegation of authority to the Attorney General, though justices debated the non-delegation doctrine.

name: Rucho v. Common Cause
description: Ruled that claims of partisan gerrymandering are non-justiciable political questions.

name: Timbs v. Indiana
description: Formally incorporated the 8th Amendment's protection against excessive fines against state and local governments.

name: Seila Law LLC v. CFPB
description: Held that an agency with a single director removable only for cause violates the separation of powers.

name: Trump v. Vance
description: Held that the Supremacy Clause does not preclude a state grand jury subpoena for a President's records.

name: Fulton v. City of Philadelphia
description: Held that Philadelphia's refusal to contract with a Catholic agency violated the Free Exercise Clause.

name: California v. Texas
description: Held that plaintiffs lacked standing to challenge the ACA after the mandate penalty was zeroed out.

name: Whole Women's Health v. Jackson
description: Addressed procedural challenges to a Texas law banned abortion through private enforcement.

name: Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization
description: Overruled Roe and Casey, returning the authority to regulate abortion to the states.

name: NY State Rifle & Pistol Ass'n v. Bruen
description: Established a history and tradition test for evaluating the constitutionality of firearm regulations.

name: Carson v. Makin
description: Held that excluding religious schools from a tuition program violated the Free Exercise Clause.

name: Egbert v. Boule
description: Held that a Bivens cause of action should not be extended to Fourth Amendment claims in border security.

name: Haaland v. Brackeen
description: Upheld the Indian Child Welfare Act against challenges related to federalism and racial classifications.

name: SFFA v. Harvard
description: Struck down race-conscious university admissions programs as a violation of the Equal Protection Clause.

name: 303 Creative LLC v. Elenis
description: Held that the First Amendment prohibits a state from forcing a designer to create content contrary to their beliefs.

name: United States v. Texas
description: Held that states lacked standing to challenge federal immigration enforcement guidelines.

name: National Pork Producers Council v. Ross
description: Upheld California's animal welfare regulations against a Dormant Commerce Clause challenge.

name: Trump v. United States
description: Established that former Presidents have broad immunity from criminal prosecution for official acts.

name: United States v. Rahimi
description: Upheld firearm restrictions for those under domestic violence restraining orders under the Second Amendment.

name: Jarkesy v. SEC
description: Held that agencies cannot adjudicate certain fraud claims without a jury trial.

name: Sheetz v. County of El Dorado
description: Held that legislative exactions are subject to constitutional nexus and proportionality tests.

name: Mahmoud v. Taylor
description: Addressed whether state mandates for inclusive curricula infringed upon parents' free exercise rights.

name: United States v. Skrmetti
description: Upheld a state law banning gender-affirming care for minors, finding no violation of equal protection.

name: Trump v. CASA, Inc.
description: Restricted the power of federal courts to issue universal injunctions against federal executive actions.

name: Louisiana v. Callais
description: Considered whether the creation of majority-Black districts constitutes unconstitutional racial gerrymandering.

name: Trump v. Barbara
description: Addressed presidential immunity regarding private civil litigation for conduct prior to taking office.

name: Chiles v. Salazar
description: Evaluated whether state bans on conversion therapy for minors violate the speech rights of therapists.

name: Trump v. Cook
description: Examines the President's power to remove independent agency heads and the scope of bank independence.

name: Trump v. Slaughter
description: Challenges the President's removal power over independent commissioners.

name: United States v. O'Brien
description: Established a test for regulating expressive conduct, holding that the government may prohibit draft card burning to protect the administrative need for the draft.

name: Tinker v. Des Moines Independent Community School District
description: Held that students do not shed their constitutional rights to freedom of speech at the schoolhouse gate.

name: Wisconsin v. Yoder
description: Held that Amish parents' right to the free exercise of religion outweighed the state's interest in compelling school attendance beyond the eighth grade.

name: Cleburne v. Cleburne Living Center, Inc.
description: Ruled that intellectual disability is not a suspect classification, but struck down a zoning ordinance based on irrational prejudice using the rational basis test.

name: South Dakota v. Dole
description: Upheld federal power to withhold highway funds from states that did not raise the drinking age, establishing limits on conditional spending.

name: Employment Division v. Smith
description: Held that the state could deny unemployment benefits to individuals who used peyote for religious purposes, as the law was a neutral law of general applicability.

name: R.A.V. v. City of St. Paul
description: Struck down a bias-motivated crime ordinance as unconstitutional content-based discrimination under the First Amendment.

name: Shaw v. Reno
description: Held that redistricting based on race must be held to a standard of strict scrutiny under the Equal Protection Clause.

name: Seminole Tribe of Florida v. Florida
description: Held that Congress could not use its Article I powers to abrogate state sovereign immunity.

name: Gratz v. Bollinger
description: Struck down a university's point-based undergraduate admissions policy as not being sufficiently narrowly tailored to achieve diversity.

name: Grutter v. Bollinger
description: Upheld a law school's use of race as a holistic factor in admissions, finding a compelling interest in the educational benefits of diversity.

name: McCreary County v. ACLU of Kentucky
description: Held that the display of the Ten Commandments in two county courthouses violated the Establishment Clause because their purpose was religious.

name: Van Orden v. Perry
description: Upheld a Ten Commandments monument on the grounds of a state capitol, finding it had a historical and secular significance.

name: Snyder v. Phelps
description: Held that the First Amendment shields those who stage a protest at the funeral of a military service member from tort liability.

name: Town of Greece v. Galloway
description: Held that a town board's practice of beginning legislative sessions with a sectarian prayer did not violate the Establishment Clause.

name: NLRB v. Noel Canning
description: Held that the President's recess appointment power applies to both inter-session and intra-session recesses but is limited by the duration of the recess.

name: American Legion v. American Humanist Association
description: Held that a large cross serving as a war memorial did not violate the Establishment Clause, emphasizing historical significance and tradition.
